newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures extends rally, gas oil ends strong.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures extends rally, gas oil ends strong.

text.p: IPE Brent Blend crude oil and gas oil futures extended a technically-inspired rally, hitting the day's highs in thin late afternoon trade.

Brokers said the market got a late boost when low-volume buying pushed November crude on the NYMEX to hit technical buy stops at $23.70 and enable November Brent on the IPE to fill a technical gap between $22.55-$22.60.
At 1645 GMT, November Brent stood up 44 cents on the day at $22.70, well above its intraday low of $22.32 hit at the open.
Earlier, October gas oil closed at $223 a tonne, up $5 from yesterday's close and not far from the day's high of $223.50.

"This latest blip higher was purely technical. A trader just But this broker and others said there were also some bullish supply-demand fundamentals behind the market's strength. Leading the way was strong heating oil demand both sides of the Atlantic amid low stocks and the onset of colder weather.
U.S. analysts said the first chill of winter was felt on Monday in the U.S. northeast, the world's biggest heating oil market.
"The people in the northeast had to turn on the heat for the first time yesterday. The heating season has commenced," said Michael Rothman, senior energy analyst at Merrill Lynch in New York.

Also lending support was concern over the health of Russian leader Boris Yeltsin and Iranian threats to the United States. Russia is the world's third largest oil producer and a major supplier of oil and gas to Europe while Iran is OPEC's second largest oil producer.
